tools.name: scope_check
tools.description: Determine whether NIS2 (and its national transposition) applies to an organization, and whether it is an essential or important entity. Inputs: EU/EEA country (ISO-2), primary NIS2 sector, headcount, turnover/balance sheet in M EUR, size-independent types (DNS, TLD, trust services, public electronic communications; cloud, data-centre and CDN providers follow the size test), and whether the organization provides managed security services (essential from the small-enterprise size in Poland, and when medium-sized in Romania). Returns classification, reasoning, the national transposition law with its deviations, and next-step links.

country.description: ISO-2 country code of the organization (e.g. IT, PL, FR)

sector.description: Primary NIS2 sector id (see the sector list in the tool description)

annual_turnover_meur.description: Annual turnover in millions of EUR

cloud_provider.description: Cloud computing provider: Annex I digital infrastructure, size-tested like any other entity (not size-independent)

public_ecn_provider.description: Provider of public electronic communications networks or services: in scope regardless of size, essential from medium size (Art. 3(1)(c))

trust_service_provider.description: Trust service provider (eIDAS), qualified or not: in scope regardless of size; non-qualified ones are important unless large

sole_provider.description: Sole provider of a service essential to society in its Member State

managed_security_service_provider.description: Provides managed security services (incident handling, security tests, information-system audits, security consulting). Size-tested under the directive; in Poland an essential entity from the small-enterprise size (art. 5 ust. 1 pkt 3 of the act on the national cybersecurity system); in Romania an essential entity when medium-sized (Art. 5(4) of OUG nr. 155/2024)

tools.name: transposition_status
tools.description: Current NIS2 transposition status per EU/EEA country (law, stage, competent authority, sources), from the Reglyze transposition tracker (curated + weekly auto-updated). Omit the country for the full map.

country.description: ISO-2 country code; omit for all tracked countries

tools.name: incident_deadline_formats
tools.description: NIS2 incident-notification deadlines for a country: the 24h/72h/1-month stages with their national legal basis, the competent authority/CSIRT and portal, the sector routing (a sector CSIRT or authority that receives instead of, or with, the national one; pass `sector` for the recipient of one organisation), and the national incident vocabulary (e.g. Italy's ACN IS-1..IS-4 incident typologies, which are types and not a severity scale, with their entity-class applicability).

sector.description: NIS2 sector id of the organisation. When given, `recipients` names who receives its notification: some countries route a whole sector to another body, and a rule over part of a sector comes back as a condition to check.

tools.name: compliance_status
tools.description: Requires a Reglyze API token. Returns YOUR organization's current compliance score, implementation/documentation sub-scores, open-task counts, and the national-framework per-objective view.

tools.name: documents_list
tools.description: Requires a Reglyze API token. Lists YOUR organization's compliance documents (title, type, status, current version). Metadata only, not document content.

tools.name: open_tasks
tools.description: Requires a Reglyze API token. Lists YOUR organization's open remediation tasks. Optional filters: status, severity, overdue.

tools.name: incidents_list
tools.description: Requires a Reglyze API token. Lists YOUR organization's recorded incidents (title, status, severity, detection date).
